content: The metabolism of avapritinib is influenced by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug when co-administering avapritinib with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If avoidance is not possible, the starting dose of avapritinib should be reduced. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage modifications. Quinupristin/dalfopristin can decrease the levels or effects of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora, but this interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown, so close monitoring is advised. Quinupristin/dalfopristin may increase the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and may decrease their levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Quinupristin/dalfopristin reduces the efficacy of the BCG live vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration is contraindicated, and live bacterial vaccines should only be administered after completing antibiotic treatment. Quinupristin/dalfopristin decreases biotin levels by altering intestinal flora, but this interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown, so close monitoring is advised. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of bortezomib, bosentan, budesonide, and buprenorphine (subdermal implant) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. For buprenorphine subdermal implants, patients should be monitored for signs of overmedication if CYP3A4 inhibitors are introduced. If dose adjustments are not feasible, implant removal may be required, and an alternative buprenorphine dosage form should be used. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine (long-acting injection) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Patients transitioning from transmucosal buprenorphine co-administered with CYP3A4 inhibitors to long-acting injections should be monitored for toxicity. If toxicity occurs and the CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be discontinued, the patient should transition back to a buprenorphine formulation that allows dose adjustments. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of buspirone, cannabidiol, capivasertib, carbamazepine, and clomipramine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. For capivasertib, dose reduction is recommended when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by decreasing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of adverse effects. Quinupristin/dalfopristin decreases the levels or effects of clopidogrel by inhibiting CYP3A4, which reduces clopidogrel bioactivation. Close monitoring is necessary. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of clozapine, conivaptan, conjugated estrogens (oral and vaginal), cortisone, and cyclosporine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of dapsone, daridorexant, darifenacin, darunavir, dasatinib, deflazacort, dexamethasone, diazepam (oral, buccal, and intranasal), dienogest/estradiol valerate, digoxin, dihydroergotamine (oral and intranasal), diltiazem, disopyramide, docetaxel, donepezil, doxorubicin (liposomal), dronedarone, dutasteride, efavirenz, elacestrant, eletriptan, encorafenib, entrectinib, eplerenone, ergotamine, erlotinib, erythromycin (various formulations), estradiol (oral and vaginal), estrogens (conjugated synthetic and esterified), estropipate, ethinylestradiol, etonogestrel, etravirine, eucalyptus, everolimus, felodipine, fesoterodine, finasteride, finerenone, fludrocortisone, fosamprenavir, fosaprepitant, gepirone, guanfacine, haloperidol, hydrocortisone, hydroxyprogesterone caproate, ibrutinib, ifosfamide, iloperidone, imatinib, imipramine, indinavir, infigratinib, isavuconazonium sulfate, isradipine, itraconazole, ivacaftor, ivosidenib, ixabepilone, ketoconazole, lapatinib, lefamulin, lemborexant, levamlodipine, levoketoconazole, lonafarnib, lopinavir, loratadine, and lovastatin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Depending on the drug, recommendations include avoiding co-administration, using alternative therapies, reducing doses, or closely monitoring for adverse effects or toxicity.
